On The 9 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 1310 of 2022

National Insurance Co.Ltd.
 Versus
 Smt. Shakun And Others
 Appearance:
Smt. Amrit Kaur Ruprah - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri M R Verma - Advocate for the respondent No.1.
 Order

By way of the present Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the
Insurance Company of the offending vehicle has approached this Court to challenge the order dated
20.0
1.2022 in M.A.C.C. No.84/2018 passed by the learned Additional MACT, Amarwada, District Chhindwara (M.P.).

2. The appellant has filed this appeal praying for following reliefs:-
i. Enhancement/Reduction of amount of compensation:
The entire award amount deserves to be set aside as against the appellant insurance company;

ii. Exoneration/liability of: The appellant insurance company may kindly be completely exonerated of the liability which has been saddled on it by the impugned award.
iii. Award of interest at the rate of: The interest awarded against the appellant also deserves to be set aside.
iv. Any other relief:

This Hon'ble Court be NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:54009 2 MA-1310-2022 further pleased to pass such other orders as it may deem fit under the circumstances of the case.
3. The present lis has arisen out of a road accident that took place on 04.08.2018.

Deceased Sant Kumar Dhurve, aged 35 years was driving a motorcycle when he met National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt. Shakun on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53838360/
1 with an accident involving a vehicle driven by respondent No.5 Ajay and respondent No.6 Sandeep is the owner of the vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result of accident, Sant Kumar sustained multiple injuries and succumbed to death.
The said vehicle was duly insured by the appellant/Insurance Company.
Hence, the Claim Case was filed claiming compensation of Rs.72,50,000/- along with interest before the Tribunal.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant filed a reply, denying averment of the claim on the ground that claimant has not valid driving licence.
The claim is highly inflated and in fact, it deserves to be dismissed.
A reply was also filed on the ground of contributory negligence and breach of policy conditions along with a denial of the quantum of compensation.
Seeking exoneration of the Insurance Company from liability.

The trial was put into motion and was concluded vide Award dated 20.01.2022, whereby the claim was partly allowed and awarded to the tune of Rs.16,13,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition.

5. Counsel for appellant argued at length and submitted that the learned Claims Tribunal failed to appreciate that in the criminal case there was no reference of the registration of the said motorcycle.

Even in the final report, there was no reference of t h e r e g i s t r a t i o n n u m b e r o f t h e s a i d N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-JBP:54009 3 MA-1310-2022 motorcycle.

6. Counsel for the Insurance Company argued that the respondent/claimant produced Shakun Bai (wife of the deceased) as a witness who admitted in para 6 that she was at home when the accident occurred as well as Santosh Dhurve (AW/2) admitted that he was at his home at the time of accident and, therefore, ruling out the possibility of him being eye witness.

Counsel for the Insurance Company further submitted that respondent No.1 was not having a valid driving licence and the entire case is totally false and fabricated by the respondents by colluding with each other and deserves to be dismissed in the interest of justice and also in the interest of public policy.
7. Per contra, counsel for the respondent No.1 submits that the Tribunal did not commit any error while calculating the compensation under different different heads.

8. Having heard the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and going through the material on record, it reflects that the findings recorded by the learned Claims Tribunal are based on proper appreciation of evidence and as much do not require any interreference.
Hence, this Court does not find any infirmity or perversity in the findings recorded by the learned Claims Tribunal so as to interfere in this appeal.
9. Accordingly, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
No order as to cost.
